plan.chapterName: OpenStax Precalculus 2e, chapter 9: Systems of Equations and Inequalities
plan.contextChunk: This figure shows three mutually perpendicular planes cutting through one another, drawn as flat colored parallelograms with no coordinate axes displayed. A green plane stands roughly upright facing the viewer, labeled x = 1 in matching green at its upper right. A red plane meets it at a right angle, tilted so it reads as a tall diamond passing behind and around the green sheet, labeled y = -2 in red beneath the drawing. A blue plane lies nearly horizontal and slices through both others, labeled z = 2 in blue at its right edge. The sheets overlap so each is partly hidden by the others, giving a sectioned, interlocking block in which the visible pieces alternate in color where they cross. A small black dot near the center is labeled (1, -1, 2), which conflicts with the red plane label y = -2; as drawn, the displayed point does not satisfy all three displayed plane equations. The drawing still gives geometric meaning to a system of three linear equations in three variables, but the plane label or point label must be corrected before the marked point can be treated as the simultaneous solution.

elements: green plane sheet (x = 1): a flat parallelogram standing roughly upright, facing the viewer, oriented as the YZ-plane at x = 1
red plane sheet (y = -2): a tall diamond/parallelogram oriented as the XZ-plane at y = -2, passing behind and around the green sheet at a right angle
blue plane sheet (z = 2): a near-horizontal parallelogram oriented as the XY-plane at z = 2, slicing through both other sheets
three pairwise intersection lines where the colored sheets cross (green-red, green-blue, red-blue edges visible as color boundaries)
small black dot at the common intersection point of the three planes
point label '(1, -1, 2)' with a thin leader line to the dot, placed upper-right of the dot
green equation label 'x = 1' at the upper-right corner of the green plane
red equation label 'y = -2' centered beneath the drawing
blue equation label 'z = 2' at the right edge of the blue plane
a warning badge/marker (shown only in 'as printed' mode) flagging that the dot does not lie on the red plane

interactions.label: Plane x = 1 (green)
interactions.teaches: Isolating the green sheet shows that the single equation x = 1 fixes only the x-coordinate while leaving y and z free — an entire flat sheet of solutions, not one point

interactions.label: Plane y = -2 (red)
interactions.teaches: Isolating the red sheet shows that y = -2 fixes only the y-coordinate; combined with the green sheet the two planes intersect in a line, narrowing solutions from a sheet to a line

interactions.label: Plane z = 2 (blue)
interactions.teaches: Adding the horizontal blue sheet cuts the line of the first two planes at exactly one point — three independent equations in three variables pin down a unique solution
Clicking a colored equation (or its sheet) highlights that plane and the single coordinate axis it constrains, making explicit which variable each equation controls and which two remain free

interactions.label: Label consistency
interactions.teaches: Switching between the printed figure and the two corrected versions reveals that the marked point (1, -1, 2) does NOT satisfy y = -2; a true simultaneous solution must lie on every plane at once, so either the plane label or the point label must change

demo_steps.title: As printed (inconsistent)
demo_steps.narration: All three planes are shown with the printed labels. The dot is marked (1, -1, 2) but the red plane is y = -2, so the dot visibly floats off the red sheet — a warning badge flags the conflict.

demo_steps.title: One equation = one sheet
demo_steps.narration: Hide the red and blue planes. Only the green x = 1 sheet remains: a single equation leaves a whole plane of possible points, fixing just one coordinate.

demo_steps.title: Two equations = one line
demo_steps.narration: Re-enable the red plane. The green and red sheets now meet along a single line — two equations restrict the solution set from a plane to a line.

demo_steps.title: Corrected: consistent solution
demo_steps.narration: Switch to 'Fix point: (1, -2, 2)'. The dot now sits exactly where all three sheets cross, satisfying x = 1, y = -2, and z = 2 simultaneously — the geometric meaning of solving the system.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World frame: +X screen-right, +Y screen-up, +Z the receding diagonal (standard isometric pose). Each plane is a finite parallelogram ~3.2 x 3.2 world units, centered on the common intersection point P. Green plane = YZ-sheet at x = 1 (normal along X). Red plane = XZ-sheet at y = yVal (normal along Y). Blue plane = XY-sheet at z = 2 (normal along Z). Intersection point P = (1, yVal, 2). In 'As printed' and 'Fix point' modes yVal = -2 and the dot/label are at (1, -1, 2) [as printed] or (1, -2, 2) [fixed point]; in 'Fix plane' mode yVal = -1 so the red sheet passes through (1, -1, 2). To keep the composition centered, translate the whole group so P maps near world origin (subtract P). Colors: green #2ca02c, red #d62728, blue #1f77b4, each plane rendered double-sided at ~0.92 opacity so overlaps read as interlocking sections; intersection edges drawn as slightly darker lines. Dot black #000000 radius ~0.07. Equation labels colored to match their plane; point label black with thin leader line. Warning badge red outline near the dot, visible only in 'As printed'.
interactionPlan.notes: Render each plane as a THREE.Mesh PlaneGeometry rotated to its axis-aligned orientation (green: rotateY 90deg; red: rotateX 90deg; blue: no rotation), positioned at the plane's fixed coordinate, with material.side = DoubleSide and transparent opacity ~0.92 so the sectioned interlocking look emerges from depth sorting. Toggle visibility per plane group (mesh + its label + its intersection edges). The 'correctedLabel' toggle repositions the red mesh along Y and/or the dot + point label, and toggles the warning badge. Click raycasting maps a hit on a mesh or its equation sprite to highlightPlane: brighten that plane's emissive and dim the others, and flash the constrained axis. Keep all geometry within roughly +/-2 world units after centering so the isometric framing fills ~0.7 of the frame.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World frame: +X screen-right, +Y screen-up, +Z the receding diagonal (standard isometric pose). Each plane is a finite parallelogram ~3.2 x 3.2 world units, centered on the common intersection point P. Green plane = YZ-sheet at x = 1 (normal along X). Red plane = XZ-sheet at y = yVal (normal along Y). Blue plane = XY-sheet at z = 2 (normal along Z). Intersection point P = (1, yVal, 2). In 'As printed' and 'Fix point' modes yVal = -2 and the dot/label are at (1, -1, 2) [as printed] or (1, -2, 2) [fixed point]; in 'Fix plane' mode yVal = -1 so the red sheet passes through (1, -1, 2). To keep the composition centered, translate the whole group so P maps near world origin (subtract P). Colors: green #2ca02c, red #d62728, blue #1f77b4, each plane rendered double-sided at ~0.92 opacity so overlaps read as interlocking sections; intersection edges drawn as slightly darker lines. Dot black #000000 radius ~0.07. Equation labels colored to match their plane; point label black with thin leader line. Warning badge red outline near the dot, visible only in 'As printed'.
interactionPlan.notes: Render each plane as a THREE.Mesh PlaneGeometry rotated to its axis-aligned orientation (green: rotateY 90deg; red: rotateX 90deg; blue: no rotation), positioned at the plane's fixed coordinate, with material.side = DoubleSide and transparent opacity ~0.92 so the sectioned interlocking look emerges from depth sorting. Toggle visibility per plane group (mesh + its label + its intersection edges). The 'correctedLabel' toggle repositions the red mesh along Y and/or the dot + point label, and toggles the warning badge. Click raycasting maps a hit on a mesh or its equation sprite to highlightPlane: brighten that plane's emissive and dim the others, and flash the constrained axis. Keep all geometry within roughly +/-2 world units after centering so the isometric framing fills ~0.7 of the frame.
